text:
katie: Heads-up: linkcheck failed on the localized site build for PR #1204. Several anchors are 404ing in /docs/zh and /docs/es but not in /docs/en. CI logs show different slugs generated per-locale.

docs-ci-bot: build failed: docusaurus build exit code 1
log: "Broken internal anchor: /docs/zh/guides/deploy#blue-green -> 404"
log: "Broken internal anchor: /docs/es/tutorials/quickstart#oauth-2-0 -> 404"

naveen: odd. we run the same slugifier for all locales AFAIK. Did the migration script write explicit ids or rely on generated slugs?

katie: the migration kept English pages with explicit HTML ids in a few places, but translations were authored by contributors and sometimes include punctuation or full-width characters. e.g., Chinese heading: `部署（蓝/绿）` -> slug differs depending on whether non-ascii is stripped before or after removing punctuation.

eli: yep. Docusaurus slugify behavior on unicode vs punctuation can vary by Node locale and the normalization step order. We should unify by computing canonical slugs post-translation using the same slugify function and then (a) inserting explicit ids into the built markdown, or (b) rewriting references to use the canonical slug.

zoe: separate but related: I noticed a flaky failing link on CI only on Linux runners: `/docs/guides/storage#case-SensitivePath` -> 404. On macOS-preview it passed. On Windows the file system is case-insensitive so the link matched. Looks like some links use mixed-case filenames in URLs vs on-disk file names.

jamal: thats a classic case-sensitivity mismatch. When authors link to `/docs/guides/Storage#...` but the file is `docs/guides/storage.md` the generated site may differ across platforms. We need a check that verifies link paths against the repository tree using a case-sensitive compare so CI matches prod.

naveen: proposals:
1) Add a canonical slug generator (JS) under `scripts/docs/slugify.js` that's used for: migration normalization, a GH Action `docs/slug-lint` that runs on PRs touching `docs/**`, and a `--apply` mode that injects explicit ids into markdown for ambiguous unicode headings.
2) Add a `docs/path-case-lint` action that walks `docs/**` linking references and checks on-disk path casing against links (fail if mismatch). Fast to run.
3) For localized builds, run slug-lint per-locale and emit a mapping artifact so translators can adopt canonical ids (and we can rewrite existing translated links automatically in a follow-up pass).

eli: agree. small implementation notes:
- For slugify, normalize with NFC and remove punctuation, then run `encodeURIComponent`-safe char stripping, then collapse whitespace to `-`. Use deterministic ascii fallback for non-Latin chars (strip or transliterate?) For now, keep unicode but strip punctuation so zh headings become short ascii-free slugs.
- For explicit ids, prefer human readable: e.g., `## 部署（蓝/绿）` -> add `<h2 id="部署-蓝-绿">` or better `<h2 id="deploy-blue-green-zh">` if we can compute an en fallback. That's heavier; start with direct slug.

zoe: for case-check, we should also fail on links that use percent-encoded sequences vs raw filenames (e.g., `%E2%80%8B` stealth chars). Sanitize and normalize before compare.

katie: timeline: we need a hotfix so current PR can merge. Short patch: run slug-lint in dry-run on the PR and print suggested rewrites; maintainers can manually apply the minimal explicit ids for the failing anchors. Meanwhile, open follow-up to make docs/slug-lint required.

naveen: I'll add a tiny GH Action that runs `node scripts/docs/slugify-check.js --dry-run` and posts results as a PR comment. For this PR I'll run it locally and push a small patch adding explicit ids for the three failing anchors in the translations.

docs-ci-bot: job queued: docs/slug-lint (dry-run)

jamal: once we have slug-map output we can also use it to update translation instructions so translators can include a stable `<!-- anchor:id -->` token if they want to pin a specific slug.

eli: good idea. add a CONTRIBUTING note: "If translating, include explicit HTML id or `<!-- anchor:my-id -->` in your doc to guarantee link stability across generators."

katie: OK. nate (ops) wants the site stable for the release tomorrow, so let's prioritize quick fixes: naveen patches PR, eli adds contributing blurb, zoe opens issue for case-sensitivity linter. We'll promote slug-lint to required after we run it for a week.

naveen: pushing a tiny patch now: adds explicit div ids in the three translated files and a WIP action file for dry-run slug-lint. commit: "docs(i18n): patch translated anchors + add slug-lint dry-run action"

docs-ci-bot: CI: rebuild triggered for PR #1204 (branch: fix/i18n-anchors)
docs-ci-bot: build succeeded, preview deployed -> https://deploy-preview-1204.docs.redwood.com/zh/guides/deploy#blue-green

eli: preview anchor resolves in zh and es. I'll draft the CONTRIBUTING snippet and push it to docs-contrib branch.

zoe: opening issue #461: "docs: add case-sensitive path lint for docs links" with repro and suggested script.

katie: thanks all. follow-up checklist:
- [x] naveen: hotfix translations (done)
- [ ] naveen: merge slug-lint dry-run action PR (non-blocking)
- [ ] zoe: implement case-sensitivity linter and open PR
- [ ] eli: update CONTRIBUTING with translation anchor guidance
- [ ] katie: promote slug-lint to required after 1 week of runs

katie: closing thread, will re-open if anything else crops up. :white_check_mark:
